subject: science
passage: In 1930 Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar left Madras, India, by ship to begin graduate study at the University of Cambridge in England. Only nineteen years old and working through the long voyage with little more than pen and paper, ______ That mass, now known as the Chandrasekhar limit and estimated at about 1.4 times the mass of the Sun, became one of the cornerstones of the modern theory of how stars die.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the calculation that Chandrasekhar completed showed that a white dwarf star above a certain mass cannot support itself against its own gravity.
choices.B: Chandrasekhar's calculation showed that a white dwarf star above a certain mass cannot support itself against its own gravity.
choices.C: a white dwarf star above a certain mass, Chandrasekhar calculated, cannot support itself against its own gravity.
choices.D: Chandrasekhar calculated that a white dwarf star above a certain mass cannot support itself against its own gravity.

explanation.why: The introductory modifier "Only nineteen years old and working through the long voyage with little more than pen and paper" describes a person, the young scientist. The noun right after the comma must therefore be Chandrasekhar himself, used as the subject, not his calculation and not a star.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject is "the calculation," so the sentence says a calculation was nineteen years old and working with pen and paper.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Although Chandrasekhar's name appears first, it is a possessive; the subject is "calculation," so the modifier still describes the calculation, not the person.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The subject "a white dwarf star" comes right after the modifier, so the sentence says a star was nineteen years old and on a voyage; the interrupting "Chandrasekhar calculated" doesn't fix this.
explanation.D: Correct. "Chandrasekhar" is the subject and comes right after the modifier, so he is clearly the one who was nineteen and working during the voyage.
